statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of four public templates plus an unavailable-item recovery state. Consent was rejected before storefront evidence capture.

page.notes: Public Chrome Web Store catalog. Home, listing, collection and extension detail templates are server rendered and enhanced client-side.

evidenceUsed: Lighthouse (attempted; redirected to unsupported consent surface and not used for verdicts)

checkOutcomes.method: Targeted screenshot/layout/DOM/network probe for respects-color-scheme
checkOutcomes.evidence: Paired desktop screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-equivalent in palette; the DOM reports body color-scheme: light.

checkOutcomes.method: Active visual/objective probe mapped specifically to respects-reduced-motion

checkOutcomes.method: Targeted screenshot/layout/DOM/network probe for view-transitions

paths.description: Discover homepage and primary extension-discovery entry point; tested desktop, 360px, dark, contrast and reduced-motion conditions.
Dark Reader extension representing product/detail and Add to Chrome journey.
The future of writing collection representing editorial collection/list template.
Invalid extension detail representing unavailable/network-like recovery state.

findings.summary: The storefront is fixed to a light theme even when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: Paired desktop screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-equivalent in palette; the DOM reports body color-scheme: light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint page surfaces, text, controls, imagery and browser UI with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The home, category and collection templates force a desktop-width canvas on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout probes measured 920px horizontal overflow on home and collection and 889px on category; the mobile screenshot shows clipped headings, cards and navigation. The detail template does reflow correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove minimum desktop widths and make the shell, hero, category cards and grids intrinsically responsive; preserve the already-working detail-page reflow.

findings.summary: The home template shifts substantially during mobile load.
findings.evidence: The 360px layout observer recorded CLS 0.5275 from a shift at about 2372ms, far above the 0.1 good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the late hero/grid geometry change and reserve its final space; align fallback font metrics and avoid switching viewport/layout widths after load.

findings.summary: Image dimensions and responsive delivery are incomplete, especially on extension detail pages.
findings.evidence: The images probe found all 36 detail-page images lacked width/height attributes, 13 were over 2x displayed size, 7 lacked srcset and 3 used legacy formats; listing templates also omitted dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio, request display-appropriate variants through srcset/sizes, and use modern formats for screenshots and thumbnails.

findings.summary: The home, category and collection templates omit a standard meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found descriptive titles and canonicals but no meta[name=description] on these three templates; only the detail page provided one. The raw home HTML contains only og:description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique meta description to every public template, aligned with the visible page purpose.

findings.summary: Extension detail pages provide Open Graph tags but no machine-readable product/software structured data.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found seven Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks on a rich software-item page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org SoftwareApplication JSON-LD derived from the visible extension name, rating, publisher, description and offer state.

findings.summary: The browser defense policy has avoidable gaps.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found CSP permits unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval and no explicit Referrer-Policy; HSTS was not present in the response. Trusted Types, nosniff and frame denial were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval and non-nonced inline script dependencies, set a restrictive Referrer-Policy, and verify HSTS is intentionally inherited/preloaded or emit it explicitly.

findings.summary: The anonymous storefront loads a broad third-party and analytics footprint after consent rejection.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed nine third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; the resource probe captured repeated play.google.com logging plus a GA page_view.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each background logging and analytics request, remove nonessential collection, and batch or defer telemetry with consent and purpose limits.

findings.summary: Cross-page navigation does not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across all four templates found no view-transition rules or declarations; navigation between listings and details is a full abrupt document swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions for listing-to-detail navigation with reduced-motion handling and a non-supporting-browser fallback.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide static chrome with no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The 5,356px-tall home page has a static header and no scroll timeline/progress signal in CSS inspection; screenshots show no progress or responsive header state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky header with a compact scrolled state or a subtle progress/scrollability cue, implemented declaratively and disabled for reduced motion as needed.

findings.summary: Below-fold media is fetched eagerly across listing templates.
findings.evidence: The images probe found 24 below-fold category images and 17 below-fold collection images without loading=lazy; the home resource probe transferred about 1.4MB across 95 resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold cards, preserve dimensions, and defer non-visible carousel/list content until it approaches the viewport.

findings.summary: Several footer links have undersized pointer targets.
findings.evidence: The target-size probe measured five footer links at only 18px high on home/category/collection and 18–20px on detail, below the 24px WCAG 2.2 minimum target size.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase inline-block padding or minimum block-size so each footer link has at least a 24x24 CSS-pixel hit area without crowding adjacent targets.
